problems.quote: a steeper indexed line indicates a higher growth rate regardless of the original magnitude
problems.problem: The slope of an indexed series (base year = 100) equals 100 × (absolute change) / (base value). Growth rate equals (absolute change) / (previous period value). These differ by a factor of (previous value / base value). A steeper slope reflects larger absolute change relative to base, not necessarily
problems.correction: a steeper indexed line indicates a larger absolute change relative to the base year, not necessarily a higher growth rate
problems.verifierReason: Index slope = 100×ΔV/Base; growth rate = ΔV/V_prev. Ratio = V_prev/Base ≠ 1 generally.

problems.quote: Countries such as Denmark and Sweden retain opt‑outs despite meeting criteria.
problems.problem: Sweden does not have a formal opt‑out from the euro; it is legally obliged to adopt the euro once it meets the convergence criteria but has chosen not to join ERM II.
problems.correction: Denmark retains an opt‑out; Sweden has not joined ERM II.
problems.verifierReason: Sweden has no formal euro opt-out; it avoids ERM II. Denmark has opt-out.

problems.quote: The annual sinking‑fund deposit is P × CRF .
problems.problem: The sinking-fund deposit uses the sinking fund factor (SFF = r/[(1+r)^n-1]), not the capital recovery factor (CRF = r(1+r)^n/[(1+r)^n-1]). CRF gives the total annual outlay (interest + deposit).
problems.correction: The annual sinking‑fund deposit is P × r/[(1+r)^n−1].
problems.verifierReason: Sinking fund deposit uses SFF (r/[(1+r)^n-1]), not CRF. Correction is accurate.

problems.quote: At noon, the sun is directly overhead, so there is no shadow.
problems.problem: The sun is directly overhead only at the subsolar point (between the Tropics); at most latitudes the sun is not overhead at noon, so shadows exist.
problems.correction: At solar noon, the sun is at its highest altitude; shadows are shortest but not zero except at the subsolar point.
problems.verifierReason: Original incorrectly states sun overhead at noon everywhere; correction correctly describes subsolar point exception.

problems.quote: At solar noon in the northern hemisphere the Sun is due South, so shadows point North.
problems.problem: This is only true for latitudes north of the Tropic of Cancer; in the tropics the Sun can be overhead or to the north at solar noon.
problems.correction: At solar noon in the northern hemisphere north of the Tropic of Cancer, the Sun is due South; in the tropics the Sun's azimuth varies.
problems.verifierReason: Original ignores tropics where sun can be north at noon; correction adds latitude condition.

problems.quote: For a morning problem at 09:00 local solar time, the Sun’s azimuth is 090° – 45° = 045° (North‑East), so shadows fall towards 225° (South‑West).
problems.problem: In the northern hemisphere, at 09:00 the Sun's azimuth is approximately 135° (South‑East), not 045°; the calculation uses an incorrect reference.
problems.correction: For a morning problem at 09:00 local solar time in the northern hemisphere, the Sun’s azimuth is approximately 135° (South‑East), so shadows fall towards 315° (North‑West).
problems.verifierReason: At 09:00 LST in northern hemisphere, sun azimuth ~135° (SE), not 045°; correction fixes hemisphere and azimuth.

problems.problem: In the northern hemisphere, at 10:00 am the Sun's azimuth is approximately 150° (South‑East), not 060°.
problems.verifierReason: At 10:00 LST in northern hemisphere, sun azimuth ~150° (SE), not 060°; correction fixes azimuth.
